headline: EDC split coverage is MEASURABILITY, not file existence, over a pool pinned by FROZEN MEMBERSHIP, not by a live re-read and not by cardinality. Over the 98 units the registry enumerates, 90 are covered and 8 are not: 1 carries no split (las_vegas/2026), 6 carry a split whose holdout is EMPTY, and 1 carries a split that no longer partitions its own graph (milton_keynes/2015). A has-a-split-FILE predicate certifies 97 of 98 and hides the last seven. The r10 v3 re-cut is complete for the class it targeted (0 closures without a v3, 0 v3 files whose closure went empty) and the 47 units still on v2 are provably correct -- but so are the 49 v3 units, re-derived here for the first time. NO split file was written by this campaign and no GPU work was spawned.

question.asked: 97 split_v2 vs 50 split_v3 on disk. Are the 47 editions holding a v2 and no v3 correctly on v2, or is the migration simply incomplete?
question.answered_with: the loader the engine resolves TODAY (pipeline.split.load_split / load_id_map), run over every edition the registry enumerates -- not the count that was true when the r10 sweep ran
question.verdict: correctly on v2, proven by re-derivation over ALL 97 split-carrying units rather than by assertion -- and the question turned out to be the smaller half of the finding

repair_round.why_this_block_exists_in_this_shape: A previous revision of this same landing was reviewed and found defective in three places. All three are now closed and each has a permanent probe; they are recorded here because every one of them was a sentence in the receipt that read as a strength.

defect_1_the_membership_pin_was_a_NO_OP.claimed: 'Two readers deliberately' -- an expected slug set read from `_registry_units(C.load_editions("edc"))`, one call BELOW `iter_editions`, so that a swapped registry could not prove itself.
defect_1_the_membership_pin_was_a_NO_OP.measured: `iter_editions(only=None, with_raw=False)` applies no filter and yields exactly one Ed per `_registry_units` tuple, so the two readers were the SAME computation. Under a real registry edit -- configs/editions_edc.json loses orlando/2014 and gains newcity/2027, which moves BOTH readers -- the symmetric difference between the rows and the expected set was [] and the coverage assertion stayed GREEN with orlando/2014 silently out of the estimand. Transcript, measured on the shipped block by this campaign: `shipped _edc_registry_slugs() size: 98  symmetric difference vs rows: []` / `gaps(shipped) = []` / `gaps(circular) = []` / `gaps(shipped) == gaps(circular) -> True`. The previous revision's own cannot-fail probe for this (replace the second reader with a circular one and watch the catch disappear) established NOTHING for the same reason: it was true only because that probe monkeypatched `iter_editions`, a route no registry edit takes.
defect_1_the_membership_pin_was_a_NO_OP.severity: the only FALSE-GREEN in the batch, and reachable by an ordinary config edit rather than only forward-reachable
defect_1_the_membership_pin_was_a_NO_OP.fix: EDC_REGISTRY_SLUGS -- a frozen 98-entry constant. `_edc_registry_slugs()` is DELETED. A constant is the only thing a registry edit cannot move.
defect_1_the_membership_pin_was_a_NO_OP.permanent_probe: test_a_constant_size_registry_swap_names_the_departed_unit performs exactly that edit against a throwaway symlink DATA root and asserts the coverage failure text contains POOL_MEMBERSHIP_DRIFT: left=['orlando/2014'] arrived=['newcity/2027']. Restore a live re-read and the probe goes RED with 'POOL_MEMBERSHIP_DRIFT IS A NO-OP'.

defect_2_the_two_readers_graded_differen.claimed: 'Two mechanical readers of the same files.'
defect_2_the_two_readers_graded_differen.measured: They were not the same files. `test_declared_zero_holdout_matches_the_engines_own_split_postcondition` enumerated `for v in ("v2", "v3")` and opened 147 VERSION FILES, while `_edc_coverage_rows` graded the 97 WINNING manifests. The two agreed at HEAD only by accident (both rejection sets are the identical six; superseded v2 manifests that fail integrity today: none).
defect_2_the_two_readers_graded_differen.consequence: Split versions are IMMUTABLE, so this block's own named repair for the six zero-holdout units -- a frac/floor policy, which must be authored as a v3 -- leaves the failing v2 on disk forever and NO value of EDC_DECLARED_ZERO_HOLDOUT makes both assertions green. Measured on the shipped block with a healthy floored v3 authored for denver/2008 in a scratch DATA root (5 current ids, v2 holdout 0, v3 train 4 / holdout 1, realized frac 0.2000, `_split_integrity_ok(v2)=False`, `_split_integrity_ok(v3)=True`, `load_split` resolves v3): KEPT -> coverage RED / postcondition GREEN; REMOVED -> coverage GREEN / postcondition RED; SATISFYING DECLARATION EXISTS: False []. The coverage message told the operator to make the exact edit its sibling assertion then rejected.
defect_2_the_two_readers_graded_differen.fix: `_winning_split_path` is now the ONE owner of 'which manifest is this unit's split', and the postcondition reader resolves through it. Same scratch fixture on the repaired block: KEPT -> RED/RED, REMOVED -> GREEN/GREEN, SATISFYING DECLARATION EXISTS: True ['REMOVED'].
defect_2_the_two_readers_graded_differen.measured_no_op_at_HEAD: all-versions rejection set and winner-only rejection set are the identical six; IDENTICAL ON HEAD: True. The change moves nothing today and is the sole fix for the deadlock.
defect_2_the_two_readers_graded_differen.permanent_probe: the same test asserts the (slug, version) pairs `_winning_split_path` resolves equal the pairs `load_split` resolves, over a non-empty compared set of 97 units. Restoring a hand-ordered ("v2", "v3") walk names every dual-series unit.

defect_3_the_tightness_predicates_were_A.claimed: an earlier repair added `not row["overlap"]` to the EDC_DECLARED_STALE_SPLIT tightness predicate and reported the wrong-advice class closed
defect_3_the_tightness_predicates_were_A.measured: the guard was added to ONE of the two predicates. On a row with holdout 4 and overlap 4 -- a manifest whose every held-out fact was trained on -- the shipped block emitted TWO gaps: the leak, AND 'STALE_EXEMPTION a/1: now has a non-empty holdout - remove it from EDC_DECLARED_ZERO_HOLDOUT'. Verbatim the wrong-advice class the sibling guard exists for, one predicate over.
defect_3_the_tightness_predicates_were_A.fix: the same term on the zero-holdout tightness predicate. Repaired: ONE gap, the leak alone, for BOTH declaration settings. The SPLITLESS tightness message ('now carries a split') is correct on a leaky row and deliberately keeps no guard.
defect_3_the_tightness_predicates_were_A.no_live_effect: milton_keynes/2015 has overlap 0 and the live leak census is 0 over 97 manifests, so no verdict on the real tree changes.

repair_round.process_defect_two_revisions_under_one_i: Two different revisions of this landing were live at the same time -- the 622-line block four reviewers read, and an unreviewed 644-line variant that closed the membership defect and left the deadlock and the asymmetry open. Landing the unreviewed one would have shipped two of three defects while discarding four reviewers' verification. The rule that follows is mechanical: one content hash per item id, verified by whoever applies it.
what_this_round_added_that_no_reviewer_d: ONE OWNER for the LEAKED_HOLDOUT sentence (`_leaked_holdout_gap`). It was authored twice, independently, in the verdict function and in the re-derivation test, rendering identically only by coincidence; nothing compared them, so a one-sided edit was silent. Both readers are now asserted to hold no private string literal naming the class, so a re-inlined copy is a RED rather than a second source of truth.

PAIRWISE-DISJOINT declaration sets. The ordering guard read `EDC_DECLARED_STALE_SPLIT <= leak_checked | EDC_DECLARED_SPLITLESS`; that union term existed only to tolerate a unit declared BOTH stale and splitless, and tolerating it also blunted the guard, since a splitless unit can never be disjointness-checked. The incoherent state is now named instead of absorbed, and the ordering guard reads `<= leak_checked`.

A PURE ROW BUILDER (`_split_row`) with its own red-green proof. overlap, unassigned and orphan are ALL 0 for every unit on the live tree, so no tree-reading assertion could show any of the three is derived from the manifest at all -- force one to a constant and every other test in the file stayed green. Measured: with `overlap`, `unassigned` or `orphan` pinned to 0, the file is now RED in each case. This is the only place `orphan` is exercised by anything in the repo.

pool_correction.why: iter_editions('edc', with_raw=False) and plan_install both enumerate 98 city/year units from configs/editions_edc.json. 97 is the count of units carrying a splits/ directory -- the ANSWER being measured, not the denominator to measure it over. A pool defined by having a splits/ dir structurally cannot contain a unit that has none.
pool_correction.second_over_pin_found_in_review: Correcting the POOL and then defining the PREDICATE as 'carries a split file' reproduces the identical shape one level down. The predicate was the real ceiling: a unit can carry a manifest and still contribute nothing measurable. Seven such units exist and all of them read COVERED under file existence.
pool_correction.third_over_pin_found_in_the_NEXT_review: Pinning the corrected pool by its CARDINALITY reproduces the shape a third time. EDC_REGISTRY_COUNT = 98 is an equality, which makes growth and shrinkage loud -- and lets one unit leave while another arrives, holding 98, printing an identical census line, and silently dropping the departed unit from the estimand.
pool_correction.fourth_over_pin_found_in_the_ROUND_AFTER: Answering the swap with a LIVE second reader of the registry reproduces the shape a fourth time, and this one was a total no-op rather than a partial fix: both readers consume `C.load_editions`, so the edit that moves the pool moves the expected set with it. See repair_round.defect_1 for the transcript. Membership is now a FROZEN CONSTANT, which is the first pin in this sequence that the thing it measures cannot move.

coverage_definition.covered_iff: the unit (a) resolves a split, (b) carries a NON-EMPTY holdout, and (c) that manifest PARTITIONS the unit's CURRENT triple id set -- covering it (nothing unassigned, no orphans) AND splitting it (train and holdout disjoint)
coverage_definition.graded_against: the CURRENT graph -- {triple_id(t) for t in load_all_triples(ed)} versus train_ids|holdout_ids, plus train_ids&holdout_ids for the disjointness half. Never the manifest's own frozen n_triples, and never n_unique_triple_ids.
coverage_definition.which_manifest: the WINNING one, resolved by `_winning_split_path` for the path readers and by `load_split` for the manifest readers, with the two asserted to agree on (slug, version) for all 97. Superseded version files are opened by no consumer and are NOT graded; grading them made the declared-debt set a function of files outside the estimand and deadlocked the previous revision.
coverage_definition.why_disjointness_is_a_separate_term: `assigned = train_ids | holdout_ids` is a UNION and hides an overlap perfectly. A manifest whose every holdout id is also a train id reads unassigned=0, orphan=0 and looks like the healthiest unit in the corpus, while every 'held-out' fact was trained on -- the exact defect split.py's own docstring says the module exists to end. The live census is 0 leaks over the 97 split-carrying units, measured 2026-07-31; the check lands green and is a guard, not a finding.
coverage_definition.the_leak_predicate_has_THREE_pre_existin: Named here rather than left for a reviewer to find. (1) run_stage._split_integrity_ok -- `if set(train) & set(holdout): return False` -- wired as the split stage's split_integrity postcondition, so it runs only when that stage EXECUTES, over its declared output patterns. (2) scripts/pipeline/test_typed_postconditions.py:125, whose mutation table already red-green proves (1) with a 'holdout leaks into train' case. (3) scripts/eval_probes.py:138 -- `if train_ids & holdout_ids: raise ValueError('split manifest train/holdout overlap')` -- which fires only at eval time, only for units carrying probes, and is NOT declared in edc.yaml (grep -n eval_probes configs/domains/edc.yaml -> 0 hits). NONE of the three enumerates the registry and none runs at commit time. LEAKED_HOLDOUT is a fourth reader whose distinguishing property is exactly that: registry-wide, on every commit, over all 98 units including the splitless one.

pool_membership_pin.EDC_REGISTRY_SLUGS: a frozen 98-entry frozenset of the slugs this campaign measured
pool_membership_pin.digest_definition: sha1("\n".join(sorted(ed.slug for ed in iter_editions('edc', with_raw=False)))).hexdigest()[:16]
pool_membership_pin.measured: 9a490fa577736290 at engine HEAD 9cd16822 over n=98; identical for with_raw=True; and sha1 over the sorted FROZEN set is the same 16 hex characters, so no constant needed recomputing when the frozen set replaced the live reader
pool_membership_pin.membership_is_pinned_by_a_CONSTANT_not_b: The expected slug set may NOT be recomputed from the registry at run time, and it is not. An earlier revision read it from `_registry_units(C.load_editions('edc'))` on the theory that reading one call below `iter_editions` bought independence; measured, it bought nothing (repair_round.defect_1). `iter_editions(only=None, with_raw=False)` applies no filter and yields exactly one Ed per `_registry_units` tuple, so the two were one computation and a registry edit moved both. The frozen set is the only reader a registry edit cannot move.
pool_membership_pin.the_three_assertions_do_different_jobs: (1) sha1 over EDC_REGISTRY_SLUGS == EDC_REGISTRY_DIGEST -- the two constants pin each other, so a one-line edit inside a 98-entry frozenset cannot pass as arithmetic. (2) len(EDC_REGISTRY_SLUGS) == EDC_REGISTRY_COUNT. (3) sha1 over the LIVE registry == EDC_REGISTRY_DIGEST -- the only reader here that notices a registry MOVE at all, since nothing recomputes the frozen set. (3) is deliberately NOT derived from (1): computing the live digest from the frozen set would make it x == x, which is the precise circularity that made the second live reader a no-op.
pool_membership_pin.the_digest_names_nothing: It fires on any move and reports two hex strings. WHICH unit left is reported by POOL_MEMBERSHIP_DRIFT, and that difference is asserted rather than assumed: the registry-swap probe checks that the coverage message contains 'orlando/2014' and that the digest message does not.
pool_membership_pin.growth_is_permitted: a reviewable constant edit, not a wall. Registry growth, shrinkage and swaps are all allowed; they are merely no longer SILENT, and each now requires editing the frozen set AND both constants.

settled.claim: every split-carrying EDC unit reproduces bit-for-bit under its own recorded parameters, v3 closure units included -- with exactly one exception, which is declared
settled.mechanism: Only the id_map distinguishes a v3 cut from a v2 cut (split.py main: `id_map = load_id_map(...) if alias_closed else {}`; the algorithm is the same make_split_v2 for both). pipeline.split.canonical_subject is id_map.get(subject_id, subject_id), so on an EMPTY map it is the identity and a v3 cut for a v2-only unit is bit-for-bit the computation that produced the on-disk v2.

measured.the_one_differing: milton_keynes/2015 -- live_map=2, holdout on disk 4 vs re-cut 8, train on disk 39 vs re-cut 74; see stale_split_manifests

settled.what_the_narrow_form_could_not_have_foun: Re-deriving only the 47 empty-id_map units applies the instrument exactly where canonical_subject is the identity, so the assertion is f(x)==f(x). The 50 units where it CAN fail are where the single defect lives. Widening the class from 47 to 96 is what surfaced milton_keynes/2015.
settled.the_skip_that_was_narrowed: The declared-stale exemption used to be a blanket `continue` at the top of the re-derivation loop, which exempted its unit from re-derivation AND from every content check after it -- so the one declaration documented as a growing queue handed out total content blindness. A leak needs no re-cut to detect and is meaningful on a manifest whose graph moved, so disjointness now runs for EVERY manifest BEFORE any declaration-keyed skip, and an assert fires if that ordering is ever reversed.
settled.immutability_consequence: Split versions are immutable and load_split prefers v3 > v2 > v1, so authoring a v3 normally CHANGES which holdout every downstream consumer reads -- an eval-series change, never a patch. For the 47 the general rule does not bite: the cut is provably identical, so no holdout moves and no series starts. It is precisely because a v3 there adds nothing but a second label on the same cut that the 47 files are DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED.

zero_holdout_units.finding: Six units carry a split manifest whose holdout_ids is EMPTY. A has-a-split-file predicate certifies all six as covered while they contribute zero to any install-strength estimand -- the artifact's own definition of the gap, one level down from the pool correction.
zero_holdout_units.arithmetic: make_split_v2 computes target = int(len(triples) * holdout_frac). At the declared holdout_frac 0.10 every n above yields target 0, so the greedy loop takes no group and writes holdout_ids: []. NO re-cut at the declared frac can ever give these units a holdout.
zero_holdout_units.live_consequence_on_the_DECLARED_path: scripts/pipeline/generic_probes.py takes the `if sp:` branch (a manifest exists), sets gold_triples = [t for t in all_triples if triple_id(t) in sp['holdout_ids']] = [], and stamps split_label = 'held_out'. That is strictly WORSE than las_vegas/2026's honest 'trained': a held-out label over zero gold facts.

the_empty_holdout_predicate_is_NOT_new_h.correction: An earlier draft of this campaign asserted, unqualified, that 'nothing notices a manifest with an empty holdout'. That universal negative is FALSE and it was asserted without checking. It is falsified twice over, by a live code path AND by a green test that predates this campaign.
the_empty_holdout_predicate_is_NOT_new_h.existing_owner_code: run_stage._split_integrity_ok rejects an empty holdout outright -- the `not holdout` clause. Cited by SYMBOL on purpose: every line number in circulation for this function is stale (an earlier reading said run_stage.py:482, another :492, another :506), because _fact_concentration_ok was inserted above it. AS OF engine HEAD 9cd16822 the def is at run_stage.py:524 and the clause at :540; re-derive with `grep -n 'def _split_integrity_ok' scripts/run_stage.py` rather than trusting any of those numbers.
the_empty_holdout_predicate_is_NOT_new_h.existing_owner_wiring: scripts/execution_contract.py:293 wires it as the split stage's postcondition kind 'split_integrity' (this citation IS stable; verified at HEAD). build_contract('edc') emits one split_integrity postcondition per unit for the split stage.
the_empty_holdout_predicate_is_NOT_new_h.existing_owner_test: scripts/pipeline/test_typed_postconditions.py:125 test_split_integrity_rejects_leaking_and_degenerate_splits already red-green proves it; its mutation table at :143-152 contains BOTH ('empty holdout', holdout_ids=[]) and ('holdout leaks into train'), each asserted is False. So the LEAK class of this campaign's LEAKED_HOLDOUT check is also already owned at the postcondition layer.
the_empty_holdout_predicate_is_NOT_new_h.measured: over the 97 WINNING manifests -- one per split-carrying unit, the file load_split resolves -- run_stage._split_integrity_ok rejects exactly these six. SETS EQUAL to the declared set: True. THE DENOMINATORS, stated because a previous revision stated one of them wrong and the wrong number is what hid a version-scope mismatch: 98 registry units; 97 of them split-carrying; 147 version FILES on disk (97 v2 + 50 v3); 97 winning manifests. The all-versions read and the winner-only read return the identical six at HEAD, so the correction moves nothing today.
the_empty_holdout_predicate_is_NOT_new_h.why_this_campaign_is_still_not_a_duplica: the predicates exist but are UNREACHABLE AT GATE TIME. The postcondition runs only when the split stage EXECUTES, over that stage's declared output patterns. It never enumerates the registry, never sees the splitless unit, and never compares a manifest to the current graph. This block is a second, registry-wide reader that runs on every commit; the honest claim is 'unreachable at gate time', not 'unowned'.

disagreement_with_the_stage_contract.statement: EDC_DECLARED_ZERO_HOLDOUT is a DELIBERATE DISAGREEMENT with the split stage's declared postcondition, not an observation that nothing else cares. The engine's own checker classifies all six as integrity FAILURES.
disagreement_with_the_stage_contract.consequence: the split stage is UN-PASSABLE for EDC until a holdout_frac/floor policy lands. Six of its 98 declared per-unit split_integrity postconditions cannot be satisfied by any re-run at the declared frac, so these six are NOT cost-free debt -- they are a MECHANICALLY_LAUNCHABLE fact the readiness ladder should eventually carry.
disagreement_with_the_stage_contract.why_the_disposition_still_stands: the arithmetic is unchanged: int(n*0.10) == 0 for every n in {2,3,4,5,7}, so no re-cut at the declared frac produces a holdout. 'NEVER a re-cut' is now argued AGAINST a checker that says otherwise rather than asserted over its silence. The repair is a frac/floor POLICY decision or a permanent out-of-estimand declaration.
disagreement_with_the_stage_contract.pinned_so_it_cannot_drift: test_declared_zero_holdout_matches_the_engines_own_split_postcondition asserts the two readers name the same six over the same 97 files, with a mandatory vacuity assert first (a checker that rejects nothing is not a witness) and a (slug, version) agreement assert before that (two readers that resolve different manifests are not agreeing about anything). WHAT THIS PIN DOES UNDER A REPAIR, measured rather than asserted: the previous revision graded 147 version files here and DEADLOCKED -- author the floored v3 the block itself prescribes for one of the six and coverage demanded the declaration be removed while the postcondition demanded it be kept, with no satisfying value (SATISFYING DECLARATION EXISTS: False). Reading the winning manifest only, the same repair loudly and satisfiably retires exactly one declaration (KEPT -> RED/RED, REMOVED -> GREEN/GREEN).
disagreement_with_the_stage_contract.read_before_editing_either_set: _split_integrity_ok has SEVEN `return False` sites, counted over the body at run_stage.py:524 -- not a dict; train_ids/holdout_ids missing or holdout empty; train and holdout overlapping; a missing decontamination block on v2/v3; a non-zero alias-leak count or zero_alias_leaks not True; a coverage shortfall against a recorded n_unique_triple_ids; a realized frac outside the 0.5x-2.0x band. Earlier readings of this file said five and 'at least five'; both undercounted, which makes the set equality MORE brittle than either said. A new name in its verdict is therefore not necessarily a seventh empty holdout; the failure message enumerates all seven.

zero_holdout_units.evidence_that_does_NOT_discriminate: probes.jsonl emptiness. Census over all 98, re-measured by this round: 1 unit has no probes.jsonl file at all (las_vegas/2026), 73 have the file with 0 rows, 24 have rows. Empty probes are the norm in this tree and say nothing about these six. The finding stands on holdout_ids == 0 alone. (For the same reason, eval_probes.py's fail-closed guard is not the reason these six are invisible: at 0 rows split_labels == set(), so `len(split_labels) != 1` raises at scripts/eval_probes.py:130 -- note the path is scripts/, NOT scripts/pipeline/ -- and the empty-holdout raise at :136 is never reached.)
zero_holdout_units.forward_reachable: This class is not a legacy artifact of six tiny units. A FULL alias closure collapses a healthy holdout to zero: 400 triples over 40 subjects with an id_map merging all 40 to one canonical yields n_groups 1 / train 400 / holdout 0, where the same triples with an empty id_map yield n_groups 40 / train 360 / holdout 40. A single alias component is rejected wholesale by split.py's per-predicate train-side guard. Running resolve and cutting v3 -- the named next campaign -- can therefore CREATE a seventh.

next_campaign.name: cut a split for las_vegas/2026
preconditions: 1. resolve must run first. configs/domains/edc.yaml:96 declares the resolve stage gpu: true. A cut without resolve is alias-inert (empty id_map) and reproduces the exact r9 defect the v3 series exists to fix.

2. las_vegas/2026 is a PROTECTED unit. configs/domains/edc.yaml:234 lists it in protected_editions ('the gold -- hand-curated 15_structured + 25_hydrated + set_times.jsonl + confusable_groups -- not regenerable'), and run_stage.py's PROTECTED_UNITS refusal rejects any stage whose declared outputs write under data/edc/las_vegas/2026/. This is a policy refusal, not a scheduling constraint.

3. whether the cut demands a re-hydrate is UNPROVEN. The earlier claim that 25_hydrated was built from all 859 triples by generic_expand's fail-open does not describe what produced it -- EDC hydrates bespoke via rehydrate_vc1.sh and relations.jsonl does not join on triple ids at all. Establishing the contamination relationship is itself work, not an assumption to inherit.
4. it starts a NEW eval series for this unit and shifts every corpus-level holdout count. Treat as a campaign with its own receipt, not a patch.

5. it will trip 'STALE_EXEMPTION las_vegas/2026: now carries a split' -- the intended handoff: the declaration must be removed in the same change that cuts the split. It will NOT trip EDC_REGISTRY_DIGEST or POOL_MEMBERSHIP_DRIFT: the registry is unchanged, only the unit's artifacts are. Cutting a v3 will also not trip the two-reader version agreement, because both readers resolve v3.
next_campaign.trap_waiting_for_it: plan_install._split_status stats split_<declared_version>.json, and the manifest declares split at --version v2. Cutting v3 directly for this unit would leave the readiness ladder still reporting exists:false while every runtime consumer happily reads the v3. See out_of_scope_findings.plan_install_reads_the_declared_version.

declared_debt.pairwise_disjoint: asserted, not assumed. All three intersections are empty today. The ordering guard used to carry a `| EDC_DECLARED_SPLITLESS` union term whose only function was to tolerate a unit declared BOTH stale and splitless -- an incoherent state nothing else reported, and one the union also let past the guard, since a splitless unit can never be disjointness-checked. The term is gone and the incoherence is named.
declared_debt.no_declaration_set_for_leaks: LEAKED_HOLDOUT consults NO declaration set, deliberately. The live census is 0, so no set is needed, and a holdout that was trained on is not declarable debt -- it is a split that measures nothing while reporting a number.
declared_debt.tightness: every declaration is asserted in BOTH directions -- a slug that stops exhibiting its condition emits STALE_EXEMPTION naming the exact edit, so a set can neither outlive its condition nor be padded with a healthy unit. Each condition consults its OWN set, so declaring a unit in one set never buys exemption from another. BOTH the zero-holdout and the stale tightness predicates require `not overlap`: a holdout whose every id is also trained on does not retire either declaration.

four_deliberate_reversals: A cut declared gap is now RED, not green. When las_vegas/2026 is finally cut it emits 'STALE_EXEMPTION las_vegas/2026: now carries a split - remove it from EDC_DECLARED_SPLITLESS'. An exemption that outlives its condition is write-only debt that could later mask a real gap on that exact slug.

Registry GROWTH is now RED, not free, and so is a constant-size SWAP -- and the swap is now caught by NAME rather than only by a hex mismatch. EDC_REGISTRY_COUNT is an equality rather than a floor; EDC_REGISTRY_SLUGS is a frozen constant a registry edit cannot move; EDC_REGISTRY_DIGEST pins that constant and, separately, the live registry. Every direction now requires a reviewable edit to all three.

STALE_EXEMPTION for BOTH the stale set and the zero-holdout set now also requires train/holdout disjointness. Without that term the messages read 'now partitions its graph' / 'now has a non-empty holdout' about a manifest whose holdout is entirely trained on, retiring a declaration on a unit that partitions nothing.

A superseded manifest is now graded by NOBODY. Reading `for v in ("v2", "v3")` felt like more coverage and was strictly less: it made the declared-debt set a function of immutable files no consumer opens, and it deadlocked the block's own prescribed repair.
artifact.red_green: Three passes. (1) SHIPPED vs REPAIRED on the three review counterexamples: the registry swap is GREEN on the shipped block with orlando/2014 named nowhere and RED on the repair naming it; the floored-v3 deadlock reads SATISFYING DECLARATION EXISTS: False on the shipped block and True ['REMOVED'] on the repair; the 100%-leaked declared-zero-holdout row yields 2 gaps on the shipped block (including the wrong advice) and 1 on the repair, for both declaration settings. (2) Twelve source mutations, each breaking one landed piece and watching the catch disappear or the right message appear -- the hand-ordered version walk, a one-slug edit inside the 98-entry frozenset, a re-inlined divergent leak literal, an edit to the owner's literal, a both-declared unit, the leak check moved below the skip, a circular expected_slugs, the dropped overlap term, and overlap / unassigned / orphan each pinned to 0. (3) The two vacuity asserts, exercised by emptying the class each guards: as landed they are RED ('VACUOUS: the split postcondition rejected nothing', 'VACUOUS: 0 EDC units were re-derived'), with them removed the same emptied world passes GREEN.
